source_caption:
TRON: Legacy wouldn’t feel the same without the music of Daft Punk. Long before the film entered production, the duo were already passionate fans of the original TRON, and when director Joseph Kosinski met with them, he later joked that it felt like they were interviewing him rather than the other way around. They wanted to be certain the sequel would respect the spirit and legacy of the 1982 classic. 

Their involvement went far beyond creating a typical soundtrack. Daft Punk spent years developing a score that combined electronic music with a full orchestra, creating a sound that felt futuristic, emotional, and timeless all at once. Tracks like Derezzed, The Grid, and Adagio for TRON became just as memorable as the film’s visuals, with many fans considering the score one of the movie’s greatest achievements. 

Kosinski specifically wanted something different from a traditional Hollywood score and felt Daft Punk could bring the same innovation to music that the original TRON brought to visual effects. The result was a soundtrack that became iconic in its own right, helping turn TRON: Legacy into a cult favorite and proving that sometimes music isn’t just part of the movie, it becomes one of its main characters.

source_details.title: Tron: Legacy
source_details.synopsis: Tron: Legacy is a 2010 American science fiction action film directed by Joseph Kosinski, and written by Adam Horowitz and Edward Kitsis. It is the second installment in the Tron series and a sequel to Tron (1982). The film stars Jeff Bridges, Garrett Hedlund, Olivia Wilde, Bruce Boxleitner, and Michael Sheen. The story follows Kevin Flynn's adult son Sam, who responds to a message from his long-lost father and is transported into a virtual reality called "the Grid", where Sam, his father, and the program Quorra must stop the malevolent digital mirror image of Kevin Flynn, Clu, from invading the real world. Interest in creating a sequel to Tron arose after the film garnered a cult following.
